configuration.java_process_repetitions: one fresh JVM for each mode/workload/repeat
configuration.measurement_order: alternate JSON/protobuf first mode by repeat

measurement_method.end_to_end_nanos: direct nanoTime interval around parse, AST build, and getCode in the same JVM invocation

local_check.timed_parent: Python process waited for a Python child that allocated 67108864 bytes

gnu_time_evidence.local_documentation: GNU time(1) says most reported information comes from wait3(2); Linux wait4(2) returns resource usage about the waited child; getrusage(2) documents RUSAGE_CHILDREN ru_maxrss as the largest child RSS, not a process-tree maximum.

measurement_method.java_command_gnu_time_wait_rusage_maxrss: GNU time %M from wait3(2) resource usage for the directly timed Java command. On Linux, this wait usage can include the maximum RSS of a waited child, so it is not a Java-only peak and is not a summed process-tree peak.
measurement_method.java_process_vm_hwm_kib: Java reads VmHWM from /proc/self/status after JVM startup, all in-process warmups, and the measured full-pipeline sample. This is the Java process's own high-water RSS and excludes child process RSS. It is null with an unsupported status when Linux /proc is unavailable.
measurement_method.memory_rule: Keep Java VmHWM and GNU time wait-rusage values separate. They can describe overlapping work and are never added.
measurement_method.parse_nanos: FortranNativeParser.parse: starts before native process launch and ends after JSON/protobuf stream decoding and FortranJsonResult construction
measurement_method.producer_gnu_time_wait_rusage_maxrss_kib: GNU time %M from the wait resource usage for the Flang wrapper's command, recorded separately for each Flang invocation.
measurement_method.standalone_reader_time: not measured: Java consumes producer stdout while Flang is running, so subtracting producer wall time would not isolate decode work
